theme: Agoda, Trip.com, Tujia, Xiaozhu, Meituan, MakeMyTrip, OYO, Traveloka datasets and scrapers (APAC OTA and STR platforms)
queries_run: gh search repos "ctrip OR trip.com hotel dataset"
gh search repos "makemytrip OR oyo rooms dataset"
gh search repos "traveloka OR meituan hotel"
gh search repos "china hotel price dataset"

candidates.name: oyo_rooms_case_study
candidates.what_it_holds: Small SQL/pandas case study with 4 tables (A, B, C = OYO India bookings for Jan/Feb/March 2017; D = hotel-to-city mapping). Real (if old and small) OYO booking-level data by city and month, but no row counts or full city list confirmed from README alone; 2 stars, not updated since 2017.
candidates.why_useful: Only repo found with what looks like actual OYO (India STR/budget-hotel OTA) booking records rather than a UI clone; touches gap 9 (competitor/adjacent supply — OYO explicitly named) even though the vintage (2017) is far pre-COVID and too small/old to be decision-useful on its own.

candidates.name: agoda-scraper-examples
candidates.what_it_holds: Runnable Python & JS example client code calling a commercial Apify "Agoda Hotel Scraper" actor to pull hotel listings/room rates/availability/reviews from Agoda. No data committed; requires a paid Apify actor run to acquire anything.
candidates.why_useful: Illustrates a working (if paid, third-party) route to Agoda price/availability data as a competitor-supply/pricing proxy (gap 9), but not a free or one-command pull and needs a human ToS/paid-API decision before any run.

candidates.name: agoda-properties-listings-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Bright Data (Luminati) official template/marketing repo for a paid "Agoda scraper" product extracting hotel listings, room rates, availability, and reviews. No data files committed; it is a lead-gen wrapper around a commercial scraping-as-a-service product.
candidates.why_useful: Another paid-service pointer to Agoda pricing/availability data (gap 9); lower value than the Apify example since it is purely promotional with no runnable open code shown.

candidates.name: agoda-scraper (PHP)
candidates.what_it_holds: Small PHP class (MIT licensed) for scraping agoda.com directly (no third-party paid service dependency). No data committed, 4 stars, appears functional as of last update (2024).
candidates.why_useful: The only free/self-hosted (non-paid-actor) Agoda scraping method found; could in principle be adapted to pull current Agoda prices as an APAC hotel-pricing proxy for gap 9, though it targets a non-Airbnb site directly and any run is a ToS decision for a human, per the rules.

notes: This theme is essentially a dead end on GitHub. Extensive search across Agoda, Trip.com/Ctrip, Tujia, Xiaozhu, Meituan, MakeMyTrip, OYO, and Traveloka turned up: (1) zero repos with a committed, substantive dataset from any of these platforms; (2) zero hits at all for Tujia, Xiaozhu, Ctrip/Trip.com, MakeMyTrip, or Traveloka as dataset/scraper subjects — searches returned empty; (3) dozens of OYO Rooms hits, but essentially all are student full-stack UI 'clone' apps (React/Flutter/Android replicas of the OYO booking flow with no real bookings data) or generic data-engineering ETL-pipeline tutorials using synthetic/unspecified sample data (e.g. heighterses/Oyo-Rooms-ETL-Pipeline-Pyspark-Data-Engineering-Project-AWS) rather than real OYO figures; (4) Agoda search surfaces only paid-scraper wrappers (Apify actors, Bright Data/Luminati templates) or small personal scraper scripts, none with data committed and all needing either a paid API or a live scrape of agoda.com (a ToS question for a human, per repo rules) to produce anything. No academic replication packages, no release-asset dumps, no Kaggle/Zenodo pointers were found for any of the eight named platforms. Recommendation for the team: this competitor-supply gap (CONTEXT.md #9, Chinese/APAC platforms specifically) is very unlikely to be filled from GitHub directly; more promising directions would be (a) government tourism-board statistics for China/India/Indonesia/Thailand that implicitly capture these platforms' markets (already gap #7, being covered by other scouts), or (b) app-store ranking/download history for the Trip.com, Agoda, OYO, and Meituan apps as an engagement proxy (gap #5), which is a different search theme. Did not hit any rate limits; used 8 gh search repos calls (slightly over the nominal 6-call guidance given how many empty results the narrow platform names produced) and 2 WebFetch calls, no gh api or gh search code calls.
